destination.title: Cosmic expansion, dark sectors and cosmological inference
destination.question: How can observations distinguish explanations of cosmic expansion and structure, and which assumptions, dynamics and inference choices control those comparisons?
destination.summary: The original packet supplies numerical membership without an authored scientific scope. Much of it concerns expansion, dark energy and cosmological discrepancies, but shared H0 motivation or AdS terminology does not establish common mechanisms, assumptions or question identity. The proposed organization preserves those differences and provides alternate access for peripheral targets.

systems: Scalar, fluid, vacuum and compact-object dark sectors
assumptions: Datasets, priors, calibration and model assumptions remain source-specific
Quantum-gravity conjectures are conditional motivations or tests
No common spatial flatness, coupling fraction or perturbation prescription is imposed
conventions: Historical discrepancies and preferences retain their source dates
Background fits, perturbative predictions and nonlinear tests are distinct
Settings, claims and methods are not automatically independent physical questions
includes: Null results, systematic explanations and premise checks
Inference methods and related theoretical questions with qualified homes
excludes: Acceptance of numerical proximity as scientific equivalence
Universal resolution of any cosmological tension
Treating every source as evidence for the same dark-sector mechanism

destinations.title: Which components account for the observed expansion, curvature, structure, and thermal radiation of the universe?

Do astronomical observations require dynamically important dark energy, or can the inference depend on assumptions about homogeneity, the global expansion rate, primordial perturbations and matter content?

What constraints do the specified supernova, BAO, CMB and matter-power data place on time-dependent CPL equations of state for both dark matter and dark energy, and do these fluid-model constraints indicate significant departure from cold dark matter?

How much of the cosmological coincidence problem reflects the temporal parametrization used to display cosmic history, and what additional restrictions on the present matter/dark-energy ratio follow from structure formation and the ages of old stellar populations?

Can homogeneous observations of the Local Universe distinguish a shallow minimum of H(z) near z ≈ 0.07 from monotonic ΛCDM evolution, and can neutron-star-merger observations independently confirm the higher H0?

The motivating discrepancy is between a local H0 determination and a lower Planck value inferred under ΛCDM. The source asks whether a changed low-redshift expansion history can favor the local determination.
Why does freeing the enlarged cosmological parameter set remove the reported ability to constrain primordial helium abundance?

Can redshift-resolved expansion measurements and nonlinear dark-matter dynamics distinguish late-activated scalar attraction from ΛCDM? The suggested satellite tidal-tail test has not been calculated for these time-dependent models.

Can Salam–Sezgin supergravity and its string realization implement AOV fading dark matter, alleviate the paper-era distance-ladder/CMB H0 discrepancy, and remain compatible with swampland conjectures?

Which scalar or vector descriptions of late cosmic acceleration agree with reconstructed supernova expansion and inferred growth, and what follows if their dynamics continue into the future under trans-Planckian censorship?

Which late-time observations constrain the local expansion without extending distance approximations too far? The selected inputs combine direct expansion-rate information, two sufficiently low-redshift isotropic BAO points and supernova-derived normalized Hubble rates.

Could an interaction acting earlier evade the low-redshift result? The source leaves that possibility open because the leading coupling correction vanishes at linear redshift order and no CMB-compatible completion is constructed.
Can an ultralight scalar rapidly decaying into dark radiation alleviate the Hubble tension while retaining a conventional potential and a plausible ultraviolet embedding?
Could calibration or photometric systematics explain the SH0ES Hubble tension, what internal and TRGB comparisons test this possibility, and which observations would distinguish the explanations?

Could surveys detect a conjecture-compatible nonzero slope, and would exclusion forecasts survive multifield dynamics or revised cosmological tensions? The paper leaves these questions open alongside potential reconstruction and stronger theoretical thresholds.

Which observational explanations and cosmological modifications could reconcile the historical disagreement between early-Universe H0 inferences and late-Universe determinations, while remaining consistent with additional cosmological probes?

Which of seventeen proposed cosmological extensions best eases the Hubble tension when assessed with a common pipeline, comparable datasets and several statistical criteria? The intended outcome is a benchmark for future proposals, conditional on unaccounted observational systematics not explaining the discrepancy.

Can an EDE-dependent dark matter mass preserve an increased Hubble constant while reducing structure growth, and can the resulting coupling agree with the SDC expectation of positive order-one exponential sensitivity?

EDS asks how an EDE-dependent mass for all cold dark matter changes early acoustic physics and later structure formation. The sign convention makes positive c the lightening branch during the net EDE excursion.
How do ΛCDM and EDS fit the combined CMB, distance, and local-Hubble datasets, and how do ACT or an approximate DES-Y3 S8 constraint alter that comparison?

The SDC motivates additional light degrees of freedom when a scalar traverses a Planckian distance. The cosmological question is whether a chosen dark matter realization of that lightening can coexist with EDE observations.

Could interactions explain the transient importance of EDE near matter–radiation equality? The source proposes testing a variable coupled fraction, alternative scalar potentials, and a quadratic mass coupling.

What necessary conditions must small late-time departures from ΛCDM satisfy to raise the inferred Hubble constant while lowering the clustering amplitude σ8, when the CMB acoustic scale is preserved? The concrete application considers dark-energy expansion changes and an optional effective gravitational coupling.

What explains the discrepancy between locally measured and early-Universe-inferred H0, why are prerecombination modifications favored, and can early dark energy satisfy existing constraints while offering discriminating tests?

Can a late negative-to-positive cosmological-constant transition improve joint cosmological fits and simultaneously alleviate the H0, MB, S8, Ly-α, age and baryon-density discrepancies? How do Pantheon, SH0ES calibration and completed BAO measurements affect this assessment?

Can reported preferential SMBH growth relative to host stellar mass be explained by cosmological mass coupling, and could a population of similarly coupled stellar-remnant black holes supply dark energy?
Can the internal pressure of stable compact objects, particularly gravastars, source cosmological dark energy, and what motion follows if their proper masses are directly coupled to cosmic expansion?

Does restricting the Einstein–Hilbert variation to a homogeneous scale factor justify the spatially averaged cosmological equation used to connect black-hole mass growth with dark energy, when matter sources are already inhomogeneous at leading order?

Can a rapidly triggered dark-sector phase transition near matter–radiation equality address both H0 and S8 tensions, and what microscopic trigger, perturbation evolution, and neutrino-mass mechanisms can realize this framework?

Can early JWST high-redshift massive-galaxy abundances probe a negative cosmological constant combined with evolving positive-density dark energy, and can this combination increase predicted stellar mass densities?
How do departures from cold dark matter affect late-universe swampland tension, inferred neutrino radiation content, and connections to H0 tension under Gaussian-process reconstruction?

Can changes in bulk particle content produce a Casimir-driven AdS → dS transition near redshift zc ~ 2, motivating sign-switching dark energy, and must such an uplift reduce the gravitational species scale?
What constraints do first-year DESI BAO measurements place on ΛCDM, dark-energy evolution, curvature, H0 and neutrino properties, alone and with external cosmological information?

Can DESI DR1 BAO observations, reconstructed without selecting a dark-energy potential, constrain scalar-field excursions, potential slope λ and derivative-related Γ sufficiently to assess the late-time swampland criteria?

Do ACT DR6 temperature and polarization spectra, alone or combined with complementary cosmological data, favor departures from ΛCDM across primordial perturbations, recombination physics, particle properties and late-time evolution, including proposed H0 and fluctuation-amplitude remedies?
How do DESI DR2 BAO distances constrain cosmic expansion, test ΛCDM against evolving dark energy, and constrain neutrino masses when combined with external observations?

Does the DESI DR2 preference for evolving dark energy survive changes in parametrization and reconstruction method, and does it require genuine phantom crossing rather than non-crossing scalar-field dynamics?

When CPL is used beyond its physics-based thawing/freezing regime, how much do claims against currently constant vacuum energy and for phantom dark energy depend on fixing higher-order coefficients instead of marginalizing over them?

Can an AdS-associated early-dark-energy episode near recombination coexist with a low-redshift negative cosmological constant, remain compatible with the selected observations, and arise from a scalar potential containing multiple AdS minima since matter-radiation equality?

Can dilution of matter trigger a first-order transition from early to late dark energy within a scale-invariant framework also containing an inflationary plateau, and yield a preliminary cosmological fit compatible with higher local H0?

How does an SDC-inspired fractional coupling between dark matter and early dark energy change DESI-era constraints on evolving late-time dark energy, and does the answer depend on whether the EDE potential is oscillatory or runaway?

Could a proposed decihertz space interferometer measure cosmic acceleration directly through long-duration neutron-star inspiral phases, supplying information needed to break the luminosity-distance degeneracy with spatial curvature?

What is the simplest model fitting first-year WMAP TT and TE spectra, does its WMAP-only fit predict other astronomical observations, and what constraints follow when external data and additional cosmological parameters are included?

How much does a stellar-population lower bound on cosmic age tighten supernova constraints on a varying dark-energy equation of state, and what dynamical models could accommodate the suggested evolution across W = −1?

Does the low-redshift galaxy correlation function contain the predicted baryon acoustic peak, and can its acoustic and equality scales constrain cosmological distances, matter density, dark energy and spatial curvature?

Can a dynamical negative-pressure component replace Λ in flat, low-matter-density cosmologies, and can its fluctuations and equation-of-state history be distinguished through CMB anisotropy and the mass power spectrum?

Can nearby and distant Type Ia supernova luminosity distances constrain matter density, a cosmological constant, current acceleration, the expansion's fate, and cosmic age, while surviving plausible observational systematics?

What critical points and expansion histories occur in FRW universes containing dust and a negative-pressure component with constant equation of state, and how well can background observations distinguish constant from varying equations of state?

destination.title: Antibrane supersymmetry breaking, uplift and moduli dynamics
destination.question: How can antibrane supersymmetry breaking and proposed replacements be represented, embedded and tested in stabilized compactifications, and how do related gauge-theory and cosmological questions constrain their interpretation?
destination.summary: A proposed family connecting effective descriptions to their assumptions, applications and consistency tests. Membership does not assert controlled de Sitter vacua, universally valid nilpotent descriptions or equivalence among its source questions.

systems: Projected, unprojected and polarized antibrane sectors
Klebanov–Strassler throats and cascading gauge-theory descriptions
Proposed alternatives without explicit anti-D3 branes
targets: Global embedding and compatibility with stabilization
Metastability, decay and spontaneous versus explicit breaking
regimes: Four-dimensional effective theories and ten-dimensional analyses remain distinct
Small-gs|N| gauge theory, probe polarization and smeared perturbative backreaction are separate limits
Field content, fermion order and modulus truncation are source-specific
assumptions: No common existence or stability claim is imposed
A ten-dimensional condensate description is conditional where stated
Exact graph relations remain source-object context rather than automatic premises of every question
conventions: Source-specific modulus coordinates and Kähler embeddings are retained
Effective parameter scans do not establish microscopic parameter independence
includes: Challenges to effective descriptions and compactification assumptions
Comparison with antibrane-free mechanisms and cosmological applications
excludes: A universal verdict on string-theory de Sitter vacua
An all-orders certification of the brane effective action
General vacuum geometry as direct evidence for antibrane uplift

sources.title: Anti-D3 branes and moduli in non-linear supergravity

evidence.text: What four-dimensional nonlinear supergravity describes an anti-D3 brane coupled to all bulk moduli in a KKLT-type compactification, and what symmetry protection does its superpotential have against perturbative gs and α′ corrections?

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua with a Nilpotent Superfield

evidence.text: Does a proposed T-dependent modification of the KKLT nilpotent supersymmetry-breaking sector consistently define nonlinear supergravity, and does its bosonic potential actually exclude de Sitter uplift when the anti-brane tension parameter b is small but nonzero?

sources.title: Anti-D3 branes and moduli in non-linear supergravity

evidence.text: Match a real Kähler potential and holomorphic superpotential to dimensionally reduced brane kinetic, mass and uplift terms, using modular covariance and nonlinear supersymmetry. The direct flux-background brane calculation is quadratic in fermions; remaining leading-order couplings are inferred through the supergravity completion.

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua with a Nilpotent Superfield

evidence.text: The component constraints from S²=0 are used to motivate the need for a nonvanishing auxiliary/SUSY-breaking direction. The authors then locate zeros of f(T)=b+cAe^−aT and compare them with the allowed complex-modulus half-plane.

sources.title: Anti-D3 branes and moduli in non-linear supergravity

evidence.text: For non-renormalisation, assign R-charges and promote flux/dilaton symmetry-breaking parameters to spurions. Write W = G0 w(ϕα, Gs/G0), with Gs including flux spurions and X. Rescale e^φ → λe^φ, G3 → λ⁻¹G3 and Θ → λ⁻¹/²Θ, giving an overall λ⁻² action and a reorganized loop-counting argument.

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua with a Nilpotent Superfield

evidence.text: An explicit two-field bosonic potential is analyzed at angular extrema θ=0 and θ=π/a, modulo 2π/a. The stated angular stability signs are respectively bc+3aW0<0 and bc+3aW0>0.

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua with a Nilpotent Superfield

evidence.text: Large-c estimates identify competition between Ac and be^{at}; numerical examples then examine de Sitter minima and stability in both t and θ, including positive and negative c families.

sources.title: de Sitter vacua from ten dimensions

evidence.text: Do ten-dimensional equations including D7 gaugino-condensate stress-energy and anti-D3-branes reproduce the curvature and scalar potential of the four-dimensional KKLT construction, with its assumptions and approximations made explicit?

sources.title: On uplifts by warped anti‐D3‐branes

evidence.text: Does the simplest single-modulus KKLT construction admit a controlled warped anti-D3 uplift to de Sitter, assuming gaugino condensation has a ten-dimensional description, and can four-dimensional supergravity parametrizations encode the authors’ proposed obstruction?

sources.title: The Tension between 10D Supergravity and dS Uplifts

evidence.text: Can a supersymmetry-breaking uplift produce a metastable de Sitter vacuum after the compactification volume, three-form fluxes and D7 gaugino condensate respond? The paper compares four-dimensional effective potentials with integrated ten-dimensional curvature constraints.

sources.title: de Sitter decay through goldstino evaporation

evidence.text: Can membrane nucleation expose a supersymmetry-restoring instability in a nilpotent-superfield description of de Sitter uplift? The proposed EFT counterpart of anti-D3-brane decay must remove the uplifting goldstino sector rather than continuously weaken its interactions.

sources.title: Constrained superfields on metastable anti-D3-branes

evidence.text: How does anti-D3 polarization modify the goldstino and supersymmetry transformations in the KPV metastable state, and does a standard universal nilpotent-superfield description admit a strict decoupling limit?

sources.title: Constructing the Supersymmetric anti-D3-brane action in KKLT

evidence.text: How can the anti-D3-brane low-energy action in KKLT, including all worldvolume fields and background moduli, be represented by the Kähler potential, superpotential and gauge kinetic function of four-dimensional N = 1 supergravity with nonlinearly realized supersymmetry?

sources.title: Supersymmetric embedding of antibrane polarization

evidence.text: Can a linearly supersymmetric effective theory realize polarized anti-D3-branes as a metastable state with spontaneous supersymmetry breaking, and explain corrections to the low-energy nonlinear supersymmetry description?

sources.title: On the Existence of Meta-stable Vacua in Klebanov-Strassler

evidence.text: Do anti-D3 branes at the bottom of Klebanov-Strassler source a backreaction compatible with a metastable vacuum of the same supersymmetric field theory, or do their infrared boundary conditions require ultraviolet deformations of the theory?

sources.title: Warping and supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Does the supergravity Kähler correction persist in the small-gs|N| antibrane gauge theory, where the microscopic coupling to the misaligned supergravity algebra is unresolved?

sources.title: Supersymmetric anti-D3-brane action in the Kachru-Kallosh-Linde-Trivedi setup

evidence.text: Can all worldvolume fields of a single anti-D3-brane in KKLT, coupled to dynamical closed-string moduli, be represented by a four-dimensional N=1 supergravity action with spontaneously broken, nonlinearly realized supersymmetry?

sources.title: Bare-bones de Sitter vacua

evidence.text: Can anti-D3 branes supply both the uplift and the small superpotential needed for Kähler-modulus stabilization, allowing de Sitter minima without an independently introduced supersymmetry-breaking flux superpotential?

sources.title: dS Vacua and the Swampland

evidence.text: How can an anti-D3 uplift sector and a stabilized volume modulus be represented in four-dimensional supergravity?

sources.title: $ \overline{\textrm{D}3} $-branes and gaugino condensation

evidence.text: Do supersymmetry-breaking fluxes sourced by anti-D3 branes in a warped Klebanov–Strassler throat generate D7 gaugino masses large enough to invalidate Kähler-moduli stabilization by gaugino condensation?

sources.title: Moduli Stabilisation with Nilpotent Goldstino: Vacuum Structure and SUSY Breaking

evidence.text: How does a nilpotent-superfield description of warped anti-D3 uplift affect KKLT/LVS vacua, visible-sector soft terms and the stability of D3-branes at singularities?

sources.title: Emergence of Spontaneously Broken Supersymmetry on an Anti-D3-Brane in KKLT dS Vacua

evidence.text: Can the anti-D3 uplifting term be understood through spontaneously broken supersymmetry and a nilpotent goldstino multiplet, and why does an orientifolded anti-D3 produce this contribution while a D3 does not? The explicit calculation isolates the role of the fermionic Wess-Zumino term.

sources.title: Global String Embeddings for the Nilpotent Goldstino

evidence.text: Can the local anti-D3/O3 configuration with only a goldstino in its low-energy spectrum be embedded in globally consistent compact geometries, including backgrounds suitable for chiral matter and moduli stabilisation?

sources.title: String Theory Origin of Constrained Multiplets

evidence.text: Can the worldvolume fields of an (anti-)D3-brane be organized into constrained four-dimensional N=1 multiplets realizing spontaneously broken supersymmetry, including multiplets useful for cosmology?

sources.title: Constrained superfields from an anti-D3-brane in KKLT

evidence.text: Which constrained four-dimensional N=1 superfields describe anti-D3 worldvolume degrees of freedom relevant to KKLT uplift, and how far can their supersymmetric action be matched explicitly to the brane action?

sources.title: A Gravity Dual of Metastable Dynamical Supersymmetry Breaking

evidence.text: What asymptotic supergravity fields and dual operator expectation values characterize proposed metastable antibrane states in the cascading theory, and what can those data establish about exponentially small supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: $ \overline{\mathrm{D}3} $ and dS

evidence.text: Does the orientifold-projected D3/anti-D3 DBI–WZ cancellation/doubling mechanism survive in a supersymmetric curved GKP background, and does the surviving anti-D3 fermion furnish the goldstino underlying a nilpotent-superfield description of uplifting?
